A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CRPI research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete Appendices A–B support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: Sections 4 and 6 and Appendix B report original conversion experiments, reward decomposition, error correlations, parameter sensitivity, and MuJoCo and DMC benchmark results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds membrane-potential distribution measurements and computational-overhead results in Appendices B.2 and B.4.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same residual carryover, clipping, and membrane initialization procedure. The optional arithmetic implementation described in Appendix B.4 does not establish a change to the evaluated method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four vector-based MuJoCo environments and six visual DMC tasks. The added analyses reuse this coverage; language modeling and diffusion appear only as future directions.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain IF, SNM, MT, and DC conversion methods and the DMC comparators LIF, TC-LIF, and Spiking-WM. The new initialization sweep is a supplementary analysis, not an added competing method.

E3.justification: Appendix B.2 introduces five initialization settings from zero to the firing threshold for TD3/IF with T=64 on Hopper-v4; B.4 adds accumulation-operation overhead accounting. Existing benchmark budgets, rollout procedures, and the 0.1-spaced alpha search remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.2 tests the assumed final-potential distribution and its dependence on initialization. New B.4 quantifies CRPI's computational overhead. Existing reward-decomposition, error-correlation, and alpha-sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 gains uncertainty values for its cosine similarities, and Figure 1 gains ± annotations for Atari and DMC results. The five-seed protocol and existing half-standard-deviation benchmark reporting remain unchanged; additional runs are not established. The new annotations are not defined in their captions.

E6.justification: New Table 8 reports membrane-potential frequencies, including 85.1–85.3% nonpositive potentials across initializations. New Table 12 reports CRPI overhead of 0.08% for IF at T=32 and 0.69% for MT at T=2. Existing benchmark returns, performance ratios, and Table 1 means are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equations, CRPI derivation, and stated uniformity and weak initialization-dependence assumptions are retained. Appendix B.2 adds empirical evidence and interpretation, without revising the derivation or supplying a new proof.

C1.justification: The introduction narrows deployment from 'without further environment interaction' to 'without extensive environment interaction.' The central error-amplification diagnosis and CRPI contributions remain intact; abstract and conclusion terminology changes from training-free to gradient-free.

C2.justification: Appendix B.2 newly interprets negative potentials as belonging mostly to inactive, clipped neurons and applies the approximate-uniformity argument to active neurons. Section 6.5 extends the efficiency interpretation to CRPI's own overhead. Existing error-amplification and overcorrection explanations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-access URL in the abstract. Appendix B.4 describes an optional alpha grid in increments of 0.125 and implementation using shifts and accumulations. These are added access and implementation disclosures; Appendix A's architectures and technical settings are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds Qin et al. (2025) on gated recurrent spiking neurons, removes Zhang et al. (2022), and expands discussion of normalization through CARE-BN. Proxy Target and CARE-BN publication updates refer to already cited works, not newly introduced research.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized terminology and grammar edits, clarifies relative performance, adds future-work sentences, acknowledgements and an impact statement, and updates affiliations and publication text. New appendix subsections supplement the largely retained narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 8 and 12 and uncertainty annotations in Figure 1 and Table 1. Figure 3 moves, and retained MuJoCo Tables 8–10 become Tables 9–11 with associated layout reflow. The existing visual presentation is otherwise largely preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 provides useful additional support for an existing assumption and the lightweight-computation claim, adds uncertainty and code-access information, and qualifies the interaction-free deployment wording. The main results remain unchanged. The gains are limited: the assumption check covers one Hopper configuration, overhead is estimated under an optional deployment grid, and the new uncertainty annotations lack caption definitions.
